SANTA CLARA, Calif. — The Broncos’ trip to the Bay Area has turned brutal on the injury front.

After starting cornerbacks Pat Surtain II (ankle) and Riley Moss (ribs) were ruled out of the game, second-year wide receiver Pat Bryant needed a cart to the locker room after an apparent right-leg injury late in the third quarter.

Bryant hauled in a 31-yard catch-and-run from quarterback Bo Nix on third down, but was tackled from behind, and his right leg buckled awkwardly as he went to the ground.

Bryant was immediately in pain and could not put any weight on his right leg. Eventually, a cart came out and Broncos medical and training personnel loaded him onto it for transport to the locker room.

Bryant, 23, had six catches for 86 yards over Denver’s first three games and caught three passes for 47 yards on three targets Sunday when he was injured.
